prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance/transfer→screening/sortation/make-up→Outbound Load Control Desk; excludes airline loading. States: operational hold/safe stop; no explicit modes. Elements/items: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit stages flight-associated bags. Bag Tag Printer produces tags/Calibration Witness Tag; replacement requires authorized identity confirmation. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies current flight/destination/date/timing; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory→Baggage Control System (Velvet), which records alarms/presents affected routes. Transfer Bag Feeder meters transfers; Late Transfer Bag Card→Bag Reconciliation Station records flight matches/sends Bag Match Query; verifies uncertain identity/location. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) assigns lanes/authorized screening-preserving routes; produces Recovery Route Card, consulted by Maintenance Technician before post-change return-to-service. Induction Tray Conveyor meters safely. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel) records tag/image; South Gate Scanner verifies identity/produces Manual Rescan Receipt→Image Resolution Desk for approved-recapture verification. Oversize Exception Ticket→Image Resolution Desk confirms authorized position. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) sorts authorized bags/holds unresolved dispositions; Chute Occupancy Note→Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern) verifies chute capacity. Secondary Inspection Chute controls examination/retention. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor deliver controlled flows. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) maintains positions/order; Carousel Release Slip←Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms flight/position/staffing/equipment/sequence constraints. Outbound Load Control Desk verifies eligibility/reconciliation. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) secures assessment area/directs handling/produces Custody Seal Log. Security Duty Manager resolves holds/coordinates response access. Tern coordinates actors/airport security personnel/airline ground operations; approves exceptional dispositions, stops unsafe/uncertain/uncontrolled induction, communicates holds. Requirements: authorized access; legible/certain identity and attached-tag verification, otherwise physical inspection/hold/escalation; Velvet authorizes checked reentry; route/flight changes approved; record disposition/checks. Preserve bag-flight association; recovery requires location/identity/outcome/authorization agreement. Validate cutoff/routes; review earlier departures. Block unsafe/jammed/blocked/alarmed/uncleared flows; scanner faults hold feed pending assessment/disposition. Stops isolate affected routes. Technician isolates/verifies stopped motion before access/jam removal; checks jams/belts/sensors/wear, reports restart restrictions/verifies

New part:
S199: A recovery begins with a controlled inspection of the affected equipment and confirmation that bags in the area have been accounted for.
S200: If a route or flight assignment has changed, the operator obtains approval before the bag is released into the revised process.
S201: The final disposition and supporting checks are recorded so that later review can trace why the bag returned to the planned process.
S202: Restart requires confirmation that personnel are clear, guards are restored, alarms are understood, and the intended route is available.
S203: Each bag remains under controlled custody from screening release until an authorized loading handoff is confirmed.
S204: The Baggage Control System maintains the bag identity, assigned flight, screening disposition, and current handling status as the authoritative record.
S205: Staff keep bags in monitored areas and prevent access by personnel who are not assigned to the active handling task.
S206: The Induction Tray Conveyor carries only bags with readable identity data and a valid route assignment into the screening process.
S207: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter directs cleared bags to their assigned make-up destination and diverts unresolved items from normal handling.
S208: The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner must report healthy status before their screening results are relied upon for release.
S209: The Image Resolution Desk reviews images that require operator assessment and records a disposition before the bag can continue.
S210: Any unresolved screening result places the bag in a controlled hold area until the required review is complete.
S211: The Explosives Response Team assesses security events referred for specialist action and communicates the resulting disposition through approved operational channels.
S212: The Secondary Inspection Chute is kept clear of unrelated bags so that identity and custody remain unambiguous during inspection.
S213: The Security Duty Manager uses the seal log to verify that recorded custody seals remain accounted for and that any discrepancy has been escalated.
S214: A Maintenance Technician reports equipment faults that could affect bag identity, screening integrity, or controlled access before the equipment is returned to service.
S215: The Baggage Operations Supervisor confirms that outstanding holds and route exceptions have an assigned owner before authorizing continuation of processing.
S216: Orchard shall release a bag to the next handling stage only when the recorded screening disposition and assigned destination are valid.
S217: The Flight Data Gateway provides the flight and destination data used to check that the bag remains assigned to an operating departure.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
